title: Functorial Cartan--Eilenberg resolutions and filtered total complexes
statement: Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be an exact additive functor between abelian categories [def-sp-abelian]. For a bounded-below complex $K^\bullet$ in an abelian category, with $Z^q=\operatorname{Ker}(d_K^q)$, $B^{q+1}=\operatorname{Im}(d_K^q)$ and $H^q(K^\bullet)=Z^q/\operatorname{Im}(d_K^{q-1})$, a *Cartan--Eilenberg resolution* of $K^\bullet$ is a double complex $I^{\bullet,\bullet}$ [def-sp-double-complex-total], with differentials $d_I:I^{p,q}\to I^{p+1,q}$ and $d_{II}:I^{p,q}\to I^{p,q+1}$, together with a morphism of complexes $\epsilon:K^\bullet\to I^{0,\bullet}$, such that: (1) there is $i$ with $I^{p,q}=0$ for all $q<i$ and all $p$; (2) $I^{p,q}=0$ for $p<0$; (3) for each $q$ the row $(I^{\bullet,q},d_I)$, augmented by $\epsilon^q$, is an injective resolution [def-sp-injective-resolutions] of $K^q$; (4) for each $q$ the complex $\operatorname{Ker}(d_{II}:I^{\bullet,q}\to I^{\bullet,q+1})$ is an injective resolution of $Z^q$; (5) for each $q$ the complex $\operatorname{Im}(d_{II}:I^{\bullet,q}\to I^{\bullet,q+1})$ is an injective resolution of $B^{q+1}$; (6) for each $q$ the complex $H^q_{II}(I^{\bullet,\bullet})$ is an injective resolution of $H^q(K^\bullet)$. Let $K^\bullet$ be a bounded-below complex in $\mathcal A$ and $L^\bullet$ a bounded-below complex in $\mathcal B$, let $u:F(K^\bullet)\to L^\bullet$ be a morphism of complexes, and let $(I_K,\epsilon_K)$ and $(J_L,\epsilon_L)$ be Cartan--Eilenberg resolutions satisfying (1)--(6). Then there is a morphism of double complexes $\phi:F(I_K)\to J_L$ with $\phi\circ F(\epsilon_K)=\epsilon_L\circ u$; in particular for each $q$ its $q$-th row is compatible through the augmentations with $u^q$. On total complexes (defined by [def-sp-double-complex-total], with sums finite by (1) and (2)), $\operatorname{Tot}(\phi)$ is a morphism of filtered complexes for the decreasing filtration by the second degree [def-sp-filtration].

source.place: Definition Tag 015H (definition-cartan-eilenberg), Lemma Tag 015I (lemma-cartan-eilenberg), and Remark Tag 015K (remark-functorial-ss)

proof.text: For every degree $q$, decompose the bounded-below complex into the exact sequences $0\to Z^q\to K^q\to B^{q+1}\to0$ and $0\to B^q\to Z^q\to H^q(K)\to0$, and make the same decompositions for $L$. Exactness of $F$ carries these sequences and the exact augmented rows of $I_K$ to exact sequences and exact augmented rows of $F(I_K)$. The six Cartan--Eilenberg conditions stated in the item give the required injective-resolution rows for $J_L$, and for its $Z$, $B$, and $H_{II}$ pieces.

source.place: Definition Tag 015H, clauses (3)--(6), and Lemma Tag 015I

proof.text: We construct the row maps by induction on $q$, along the sequence $0\to B^q\to Z^q\to H^q\to0$, $0\to Z^q\to K^q\to B^{q+1}\to0$ of Step 1. The induction claim at $q$ is that a map $\varphi_B^q$ from the row $F(\operatorname{Im}(d_{II}:I_K^{\bullet,q-1}\to I_K^{\bullet,q}))$ to the corresponding row of $J_L$ has been constructed, compatible with the augmentations (through $u$). Below the lowest nonzero degree all rows are zero, and in the lowest degree $B^q=0$, so $\varphi_B^q=0$ starts the induction. Given $\varphi_B^q$: (a) the $H^q$ row map $\varphi_H^q$ is obtained from [lem-weil-pbc-lift-along-injective-quasi-iso], applied to the augmentation $F(H^q(K))[0]\to F(H^q_{II}(I_K))$, which is a monomorphic quasi-isomorphism because $0\to F(H^q(K))\to F(H^q_{II}(I_K)^{0})\to F(H^q_{II}(I_K)^{1})\to\cdots$ is exact, and to the map $F(H^q(K))\to H^q(L)\to H^q_{II}(J_L)^{0}$ into the bounded-below injective complex $H^q_{II}(J_L)$; (b) the $Z^q$ row map $\varphi_Z^q$ is the middle map $\varphi_B$ given by [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-morphism-lift-exact-source] for the short exact sequence of exact augmented complexes $0\to F(B^q\text{-row})\to F(Z^q\text{-row})\to F(H^q\text{-row})\to0$ over $0\to F(B^q)\to F(Z^q)\to F(H^q(K))\to0$, the target horseshoe $0\to B^q\text{-row}\to Z^q\text{-row}\to H^q_{II}\text{-row}$ of $J_L$ (injective resolutions by (4)--(6), degreewise exact, zero for $p<0$ by (2)) and the endpoint maps $\varphi_B^q,\varphi_H^q$; (c) the $B^{q+1}$ row map $\varphi_B^{q+1}$ is obtained from [lem-weil-pbc-lift-along-injective-quasi-iso] exactly as in (a), for the row $F(\operatorname{Im}(d_{II}:I_K^{\bullet,q}\to I_K^{\bullet,q+1}))$ augmented by $F(B^{q+1})$; (d) the $K^q$ row map $\phi^{\bullet,q}$ is the middle map $\varphi_B$ given by [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-morphism-lift-exact-source] for $0\to F(Z^q\text{-row})\to F(I_K^{\bullet,q})\to F(B^{q+1}\text{-row})\to0$ over $0\to F(Z^q)\to F(K^q)\to F(B^{q+1})\to0$, the target horseshoe given by (3)--(5), and the endpoint maps $\varphi_Z^q,\varphi_B^{q+1}$. Each row map is chosen exactly once: $\varphi_B$ and $\varphi_H$ by the quasi-isomorphism lift, $\varphi_Z$ and $\phi^{\bullet,q}$ as horseshoe middle maps, so the three-term compatibilities of (b) and (d) hold for the maps actually used, and $\varphi_B^{q+1}$ continues the induction.

source.place: Lemma Tag 015I, comparison morphism construction, written degree-by-degree using its cycle, boundary, and cohomology rows

proof.text: The resulting row maps commute with $d_I$ by construction. They commute with $d_{II}$ because on the $q$-th row the vertical differential factors as $I^{\bullet,q}\to J_B^{\bullet,q+1}\to J_Z^{\bullet,q+1}\to I^{\bullet,q+1}$ through the boundary and cycle rows, and every factor commutes by the induction claim, including the three-term compatibilities supplied by the exact-source horseshoe lifts. Thus the row maps assemble to a morphism of double complexes $\phi:F(I_K)\to J_L$, and the degree-zero augmentation identity is $\phi\circ F(\epsilon_K)=\epsilon_L\circ u$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 015I, proof that the comparison maps commute with the vertical differential (the composite through boundaries and cycles)

proof.text: Take the direct sum of the bidegree-preserving components $\phi^{p,q}$ in each total degree. The total differential and the decreasing filtration by the second degree are those of [def-sp-double-complex-total] and [def-sp-filtration]. Since $\phi$ commutes with both double-complex differentials and preserves bidegrees, its total map is a filtered chain map; the sums are finite by the bounded-below and nonnegative-degree conditions.
